item.title: Creating a New Theme
item.description:
Introduction

This tutorial will show you how to create a simple theme in Hugo. I assume that you are familiar with HTML, the bash command line, and that you are comfortable using Markdown to format content. I’ll explain how Hugo uses templates and how you can organize your templates to create a theme. I won’t cover using CSS to style your theme.

We’ll start with creating a new site with a very basic template. Then we’ll add in a few pages and posts. With small variations on that, you will be able to create many different types of web sites.

item.title: Migrate to Hugo from Jekyll
item.description:
Move static content to static

Jekyll has a rule that any directory not starting with _ will be copied as-is to the _site output. Hugo keeps all static content under static. You should therefore move it all there. With Jekyll, something that looked like

▾ <root>/
    ▾ images/
        logo.png

should become

▾ <root>/
    ▾ static/
        ▾ images/
            logo.png

Additionally, you’ll want any files that should reside at the root (such as CNAME) to be moved to static.

item.title: Alberto
item.description:
I’m a PhD graduate in Cognitive Neuroscience with experience in data analysis, human-subject research, and clinical research across academic, hospital, and industry settings in Europe, the US, and Japan.

My work has involved study design, participant coordination, statistical modelling, multimodal data analysis, and reporting tools using R and Python. I’ve also worked with neuroimaging, neurostimulation, behavioural research, and regulatory-compliant data in ethics-approved studies.

I’m comfortable moving between analysis, research coordination, and communication, particularly when working with people from different technical backgrounds. My experience covers both the research and operational sides of studies, from working with participants and managing research data to analysing results and communicating findings. I’m interested in opportunities at the intersection of healthcare, research, data, and technology.

item.title: Clinical Research

item.title: PairedPulse TMS Analysis
item.description:
The goal of PairedPulse TMS Analysis package is to provide a set of R functions for analysing and normalising raw paired-pulse TMS data.

I created and currently use the package to process paired-pulse measurements, organise test stimulus and conditioned stimulus responses, and apply different normalisation methods to the data. The functions can work with both wide and long data formats and can be applied to individual datasets or dataframes containing multiple participants. The package also includes functions for plotting the normalised data, allowing me to visualise the responses across different triggers and compare the results between participants.

item.title: PairedPulse TMS Visualisation
item.description:
The goal of the PairedPulseTMS Visualisation package is to provide an interactive visualisation tool for inspecting and processing paired-pulse TMS recordings exported from LabChart.

I created and currently use the package to visually inspect individual TMS pulses, scroll through recordings, and compare responses across different pulses and trials. The tool makes it possible to identify and discard trials or pulses that are unsuitable for further analysis, providing a more controlled way of cleaning the raw TMS data before subsequent processing.

item.title: SRTT Analysis
item.description:
The goal of SRTTAnalysis is to provide a set of R functions for analysing raw reaction time data, particularly data from the Serial Reaction Time Task (SRTT).

I created and currently use the package to process and filter reaction time data, calculate performance measures such as skill across different task phases, and examine the percentage of filtered values. The functions can work with both wide and long data formats and can be applied to individual datasets or dataframes containing multiple participants. The package also includes functions for plotting reaction time data and skill measures, allowing me to examine changes in performance across the different stages of an SRTT.

item.title: SRTT Distribution
item.description:
The goal of the SRTT Distribution APP package is to provide a set of R functions for exploring how different statistical distributions fit reaction time data collected during a Serial Reaction Time Task (SRTT).

I created and currently use the package to investigate how mean, variance, lag, and other distributional properties change across different sample sizes and windows of reaction time data. The package allows me to compare different fitting approaches, including the normal, gamma, and shifted log-normal distributions, and to identify which distribution provides the best fit to the observed reaction time data.

item.title: Création d'un nouveau thème
item.description:
Introduction

Ce tutoriel vous montrera comment créer un thème simple pour Hugo. Je suppose que vous êtes familier avec HTML, la ligne de commande bash, et que vous êtes à l’aise avec Markdown pour formater le contenu. Je vais expliquer comment Hugo utilise des modèles et comment vous pouvez organiser vos modèles pour créer un thème. Je ne couvrirai pas l’utilisation de CSS pour styliser votre thème.

Nous allons commencer par créer un nouveau site avec un modèle très basique. Ensuite, nous ajouterons quelques pages et des publications. Avec de petites variations, vous pourrez créer de nombreux types de sites web.

item.title: (Hu)go Template Primer
item.description:
Hugo uses the excellent Go html/template library for its template engine. It is an extremely lightweight engine that provides a very small amount of logic. In our experience that it is just the right amount of logic to be able to create a good static website. If you have used other template systems from different languages or frameworks you will find a lot of similarities in Go templates.

This document is a brief primer on using Go templates. The Go docs provide more details.

item.title: Migrer vers Hugo depuis Jekyll
item.description:
Déplacez le contenu statique vers static

Jekyll a une règle comme quoi tout répertoire qui ne commence pas par _ sera copié tel-quel dans le répertoire _site. Hugo garde tout le contenu statique dans le répertoire static. Vous devez donc déplacer tout ce type de contenu là-dedans. Avec Jekylll, l’arborescence ressemblant à ceci :

▾ <root>/
    ▾ images/
        logo.png
